newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares retreat but turnaround see soon.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares retreat but turnaround see soon.

text.p: Norwegian shares continued to retreat on Monday as investors remained cautious waiting see direction in the United States and Europe, although dealers said they saw a rebound in the near term.
Oslo's total share in dex closed 0.83 percent off at 1,055.43 points in relatively slim turnover of 973 million crowns despite the bourse extending trading time to 1600 GMT.

"Investors are staying away. The volume is lower than usual, we're waiting to see what happens in London and on Wall Street," said one broker. "But I don't think we are far from the bottom. We should see a rebound soon. There's further upside potential."
Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand continued to attract buying attention and was the most heavily traded share in turnover terms at 200 million crowns.
On Friday Storebrand accounted for 561 million crowns of the session's trade and there was speculation that a foreign buyer intended to acquire 10 percent in the company.
Financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv said on Monday it believed Norwegian billionaire entrepreneur Kjell Inge Roekke was a central figure in the deal.
